I am 61 years old, finished middle school, and I have farmed these same 10.1 mu for 40 years. With just me and my wife working the land, every yuan I spend on inputs has to count, but a bad harvest would be far worse than wasting a little fertilizer. I mostly do what worked last year and what I see my neighbors doing. Last year my wheat got about 500 kg per mu and my maize about 600 kg per mu, so this year I will keep things steady and maybe push a bit more on fertilizer.

For winter wheat, I sow in early October. I buy the improved wheat seed from the county supply store — the same kind my neighbor Li used last year, his wheat stood well. I sow about 17 jin per mu. Before sowing, I run the rotary tiller to chop up the maize stalks and make a flat seedbed. At sowing time, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 50 jin of 15-15-15. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I topdress with 30 jin of urea per mu. I would rather see a little extra green than yellow weak plants. I irrigate twice: once before winter so the wheat does not dry out, and once at jointing in April. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see aphids or rust, I spray fungicide or insecticide once more. I expect 550 kg per mu if the spring weather holds.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. I use hybrid seed, about 5 jin per mu. I do not do deep tillage — I plant no-till with the seeder so I do not lose moisture and I can finish before the rains come. I put 40 jin of compound fertilizer in the furrow at sowing. At the big trumpet stage in July, I spread another 30 jin of urea per mu. In summer it sometimes rains enough, but I irrigate once at flowering time if it turns dry, and maybe a second time if there is a long hot spell. I spray herbicide before the seedlings emerge, and I keep an eye out for corn borers — if I see them, I spray insecticide once. I expect about 650 kg per mu.

Fertilizer prices went up again this year, but I am not cutting back. I saw what happened to Old Wang two years ago when he tried to save money on urea — his maize was stunted and he lost half a season.
